title: SPUExecutionResult Contract

scope.purpose: Define the structured result returned by one normally completed Step Processing Unit invocation to its owning Step Composition.

contract.name: SPUExecutionResult
contract.responsibility: Carry the processing artifact and SPU-invocation-scoped structured results/evidence that the concrete SPU contract assigns to its invocation.
nonResponsibilities: Represent the aggregate result of the complete Step.
Define the Stage-facing Step result contract.
Own Step-level flow control or Step-level result composition.
Absorb all Step-level ErrorResult or ErrorHandlerResult aggregation merely because an SPU produced source occurrences or operation entries.

typeParameters.name: TOutput
typeParameters.meaning: The type of processing artifact produced by this concrete SPU invocation, when one is produced.

typeParameters.name: TErrorOccurrenceContext
typeParameters.meaning: The SPU-specialized context type carried by SPUError occurrences made available in this SPU invocation result, when applicable.

elements.name: processingArtifact
elements.meaning: The artifact produced by this SPU invocation.
constraints: When present, conforms exactly to the SPU's TOutput specialization.
Its semantics are defined by the concrete SPU and owning Step.
It is not automatically the Step's final TOutput.

elements.name: spuErrorOccurrences
elements.meaning: Original SPUError occurrences created by this SPU for errors arising within its own processing responsibility and made available to Step Composition.
constraints: Each occurrence preserves its occurrence identity and exact error-type-definition reference.
The producing SPU identity is associated with each occurrence when incorporated into Step-level aggregation or references.
No occurrence is synthesized merely because an exception prevented SPUExecutionResult from being returned.
The concrete Step defines whether and how these occurrences are included in its Step-level ErrorResult.

elements.name: validatorResult
elements.producer: Applicable validator unit or SPU-specific validator composition
elements.meaning: The validation result associated specifically with this SPU invocation, when the Step's design assigns such validation to this SPU scope.
constraints: Its concrete structure and composition are defined by the applicable validator contracts and Step specialization.
It is not a universal status for the SPU or Step.

optionality.rule: All elements are independently optional; absence is not a success/failure status.
semantics: Absence means the corresponding value was not included in this SPUExecutionResult.
Absence alone does not establish that a component was inapplicable, not executed, successful, or failed.
The concrete Step defines applicability and interpretation.

preservation.invariant: Every result element actually produced and available under the SPU invocation contract must be preserved in the returned SPUExecutionResult.
rules: A later internal failure must not discard an earlier result that the SPU contract requires to be returned.
No result is fabricated for an operation that did not produce one.

If an exception prevents SPUExecutionResult from being returned, previously produced evidence and results are subject to the concrete Step's separately defined recovery/retention contract; they must not be mislabeled as a returned SPUExecutionResult.
The SPU assembles only its own invocation-level result according to its specialized SPU contract.
The SPU does not assemble StepExecutionResult.
The SPU does not decide the Step's next flow transition.
The Step Composition consumes returned SPUExecutionResult values and performs any cross-SPU or Step-level aggregation.
The contract does not mandate a constructor, builder, serialization format, or memory ownership model.
An exception that prevents execute from returning is not an SPUExecutionResult.
The exception is recorded/handled according to the concrete Step and SPU exception contracts.
No universal conversion from exceptions to SPUError occurrences or structured result elements is imposed.

explicitNonGoals: No universal SPU success boolean or status is introduced.
No Step-level ErrorResult or ErrorHandlerResult aggregate is required in this contract.
No fixed order of processing, validation, error production, or observation is imposed.
No Stage-level or Pipeline-level flow policy is defined.
